title: Causal exact producer release replay on the shared Llama7B mesh
hypothesis: Feeding every measured p54/p53 output cycle into the exact shared-mesh RTL with one held beat and stall-dilated future releases will replace eager VC1 injection without introducing an unbounded trace queue.

direct_comparison.primary_question: How long does the embodied shared mesh take when exact VC1 rows become valid at measured producer cycles and downstream stalls causally delay each source?
include: all 512 measured rows from both p54 and p53 structural families
p54 mapping to endpoints 0-7 and p53 mapping to endpoints 8-15
one common synchronous clock matching the composed RTL
one held output beat per source with no hidden release queue
112 VC0 contexts, 7616 packets, and 60928 exact payload flits
four VC1 groups, 1260 packets, 10020 flits, and 512 exact root rows
cycle-by-cycle RTL versus Python endpoint VC arbitration
exclude: independent producer and mesh clocks without CDC RTL
wiring VC0 SRAM destination writes into the cluster fill plane
sixteen independently measured duplicate producer traces

supersedes: eager VC1 source-valid timing as a throughput claim
does_not_supersede: the eager 15769-cycle standalone service capacity bound
the exact VC0 and stats-once VC1 traffic quantities

required_evaluations.objective: Verify producer-release-coupled exact shared-mesh RTL and preserve split VC0/VC1 completion.

remaining_abstractions: Representative p54/p53 traces are replicated across same-structure endpoints.
Measured no-stall inter-row deltas are conservatively dilated rather than closing direct producer backpressure.
VC0 transport completion does not yet drive cluster SRAM fill residency.
HBM/DRAM remains outside the chip RTL boundary.
next_gate: Directly connect VC0 destination SRAM writes to the cluster fill interface and compose producer, reducer, and mesh valid-ready behavior without trace-derived VC1 sources.
